title: Invariance Under Register-State Equality
statement: Fix a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean input symbols, a Boolean parameter $o$, a Boolean input word $x$, a natural-number register bound $B$, a control label $l$, and a rational number $p$. For register states $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$, if $\sigma=\sigma'$ and the polynomial-amplification program initialized at $l$ with register state $\sigma'$ has all registers bounded by $B$, terminates for every sequence of choice bits, and has probabilities $p$ and $1-p$ of returning true and false, respectively, at every choice-sequence length for which all branches halt, then the same properties hold when it is initialized with $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: The register states satisfy σ = σ'

The probabilistic-semantics property holds for σ': bounded registers, termination for every choice-bit sequence, and the stated true and false probabilities at every length for which all branches halt
replaced:
Fix a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet, Boolean
parameter $o$, input word $x$, register bound $B$, control label $l$, rational number
$p$, and register records $\sigma,\sigma'$. If $\sigma=\sigma'$ and the
polynomial-amplification program started at label $l$ with the register vector encoded
by $\sigma'$, no result yet, and all registers bounded by $B$, terminates along every
sequence of choice bits and has probabilities $p$ and $1-p$ of returning true and false,
respectively, for every length at which all branches halt, then the same claim holds
when initialized from $\sigma$.
